kicker: Road Rash, read from its code

scenes.headline: How a 1996 game runs in a browser tab
scenes.sub: Old data tables, new Three.js code
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kickstand! This page rebuilds a motorcycle game from its own data tables.

scenes.text: The rebuild keeps the original's data and rules, and replaces the program. New Three.js code reads the old tables, so courses and bikes behave as they did.
scenes.say: The page keeps the original's data and rules, and replaces the program. New code reads the old tables.

scenes.title: From old bytes to a race

steps.say: Courses are lists of byte pairs, and the sprites, text and music come from the original game.
The rules are read back from the original program. The code cites fifty three addresses in it.
New code in Three.js draws the race and runs the riders by those rules.
Friend rooms and scores need a server, which the page does not show.

scenes.title: One step of road
scenes.say: A course is bytes, and each step of road turns the heading by a simple rule.

parts.note: the path byte a, as a slope
parts.say: The path byte becomes an angle.
Half of it is used for each step.

scenes.title: Seconds from 0 to 60 mph
scenes.note: our re-run of the site's bike model
scenes.say: I re-ran the bike model on a flat road. The cheapest bike takes five point two seconds to sixty, and the dearest takes three point one seven.

scenes.label: mean gap, table top vs model
scenes.note: the table's top speed is implied by its other columns
scenes.say: The table's top speed is not an input. It is what the other columns imply, within a mean gap of one point three four.

scenes.text: The engine is new and the rules are recovered, but the data is still the original's, with no licence we could find.
scenes.say: The engine is new and the rules are recovered. The data is still the original's, with no licence we could find.

recap: Top speed is implied by the table.
Rooms and scores need a server.
scenes.say: Courses are bytes, top speed follows from the table, and rooms and scores need a server.
